task_1.title: Restore Git() remote commit checks on Git versions earlier than 2.36
task_1.description: Conan 2.17.1 fixes a compatibility issue in the Git() helper so operations that check whether a commit exists in a remote continue to work on Git versions earlier than 2.36. The update preserves the expected boolean outcome for remote commit checks instead of failing because the newer probe path is not supported.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's `Git()` helper can determine whether a commit exists in a remote repository when running with Git versions earlier than 2.36, while preserving the existing success and failure contract of the remote existence check.

expectation.grounded: When `Git()` performs an operation that checks whether a commit exists in a remote, it must support both newer Git versions and git versions earlier than 2.36. If the preferred remote-check probe cannot be used, the operation should transparently retry with a compatible alternative and return `true` only when the remote commit can be confirmed; otherwise it should return `false` instead of surfacing a generic probe failure.
expectation.conceptual: Remote commit existence checks should keep working across supported Git versions. Users should receive the same observable yes or no result even on older Git installations, without changing their Conan workflow.

constraints.grounded: The compatibility fix applies specifically to `Git()` operations whose contract is to check remote commit presence. The operation must remain non-throwing for ordinary probe failures and must not report success unless the commit can actually be confirmed from the remote.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should stay limited to compatibility for remote commit detection, preserve current behavior on newer environments, and avoid turning a boolean capability check into an unexpected hard failure.

behavior: A `Git()` remote commit existence check should continue to work when the local Git client is older than 2.36.

If the preferred remote probe is unsupported or otherwise fails in a way consistent with older Git compatibility, the check should automatically fall back to an older-compatible remote fetch strategy.
The check should report success only when the target commit can be confirmed as present in the remote.
If neither probe can confirm the commit, the operation should return `false` rather than raising a generic exception from the fetch attempt.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan runs a `Git()` operation that checks whether a commit exists in a remote on Git 2.36 or newer, it should continue to produce the same boolean outcome as before.
When the same remote commit check runs on a Git version earlier than 2.36 and the commit exists in the remote, it should still report success.
When the remote commit is not available, the check should report failure as a boolean negative result instead of crashing because the probe mechanism failed.
When the first probe mechanism cannot be used because of Git version compatibility, fallback handling should happen internally and the user-visible contract should remain unchanged.
